candidate.declared_purpose: causal inference-driven functional black-box testing using causal DAGs and intervention-to-outcome test cases

paper.title: Testing Causality in Scientific Modelling Software

observed_source_architecture: CausalTestingFramework loads a causal DAG, runtime data and causal test cases, then executes configured estimators and expected causal effects.
CausalTestCase separates treatment variable, outcome variable, expected causal effect, effect measure and estimator, and records PASS/FAIL/INESTIMABLE outcomes.
ExperimentalEstimator exposes a run_system(configuration) seam for black-box interaction with the system under test.
ExperimentalEstimator constructs control_configuration and treatment_configuration from the same adjustment configuration and changes only the treatment variable.
ExperimentalEstimator can estimate average treatment effect and risk ratio by repeated control/treatment executions.
The upstream experimental-estimator unit test demonstrates the black-box seam on a deterministic SystemUnderTest and checks exact effect estimates.
The package uses plugin entry points for estimators, expected causal effects and causal discovery mechanisms.
The core dependency surface is scientific-Python heavy: networkx, numpy, pandas, scikit-learn, scipy, statsmodels, lifelines, pyarrow/fastparquet, sympy and additional search/graph packages.

strong_fit: explicit treatment-vs-control semantics map naturally to broadcast-intervention vs matched control
run_system is a useful abstraction for keeping the causal test outside the internal implementation of the subject under test
explicit expected-effect and INESTIMABLE outcomes support fail-closed causal adjudication instead of treating every difference as causal success
adjustment configuration is conceptually compatible with freezing non-broadcast inputs across matched runs
required_f2_extensions: exact causal_probe_id shared across control/intervention pair
exact BroadcastEnvelope identity on the intervention arm and explicit no-broadcast/sham identity on control
complete recipient-scoped OFFERED/DELIVERED/UPTAKEN receipt set bound to broadcast.recipient_cell_ids
generation/frame-version/provenance fences from accepted WP502/WP506 contracts
order/seed/nondeterminism controls where runtime is not deterministic
authority fence preventing statistical estimates or DAG assumptions from minting canonical truth/effects/completion

limitations_and_negative_evidence: Upstream treatment/control series are not intrinsically bound by an F2-style immutable pair identity or per-pair input digest.

The experimental estimator performs repeated control executions followed by repeated treatment executions; without an additional pairing/order/seed contract, time/order effects can masquerade as treatment effects in a stateful or stochastic target.
A causal DAG is an asserted model of expected relationships; its presence is not evidence that the asserted edge is correct.
The generic framework supports statistical inference from runtime data, whereas current WP507 G3 requires a stricter deterministic matched intervention/control contract at repository-component scope.
The dependency surface is too broad for a justified WP507 core dependency absent an E4 ablation showing benefit over a thin native comparator.
No source inspection performed here demonstrates Frankenstein 2.0 runtime integration, target-runtime execution, physical GRID10 behavior, J-Space causality or effect authority.

keep: optional adequacy/confidence machinery for a later nondeterministic runtime layer
reject_for_core: unbound aggregate treatment/control series as sufficient causal evidence
statistical significance as a substitute for exact F2 causal/provenance identity
donor_distillation.minimal_f2_native_shape: MatchedCausalProbe(control, intervention) -> verify frozen-input identity -> verify intervention identity -> verify recipient uptake completeness -> compare downstream output -> return POSITIVE|NEGATIVE|INESTIMABLE with exact receipt refs

hypotheses.statement: Distilling CITCOM's explicit treatment/control/expected-effect abstraction into a thin F2-native matched-causal-probe contract will make WP507 falsification clearer without importing hidden-state machinery.
hypotheses.falsifier: A direct WP507 test matrix shows no reduction in ambiguity, no new rejected false-positive class, and no improvement in reproducibility relative to the current native contract.

hypotheses.statement: WP507 G3 already contains all useful treatment/control semantics, so CITCOM adds naming only and should not influence implementation.
hypotheses.discriminator: Diff the accepted future WP507 test matrix against current G3 requirements and count whether explicit INESTIMABLE/order/nondeterminism/model-assumption cases add a genuinely new fail-closed class.

hypotheses.statement: Statistical causal machinery is actively harmful at the current deterministic contract layer because it can weaken exact provenance requirements.
hypotheses.discriminator: Attempt a thin native probe design and reject any variant that permits an effect estimate when pair identity, frozen-input digest, broadcast identity or uptake completeness is missing.

next_discriminator.proposal: Add a tiny deterministic fixture around the native WP507 contract with at least four false-positive cases: mismatched non-broadcast digest, incomplete recipient uptake, changed output under sham/no-broadcast arm, and order/state contamination. Only consider an E4 integration ablation if that fixture exposes a real current gap.
